tools.name: list_block_types
tools.label: List block types
tools.description: Registered block types with per-block `preference` (tier + replacement), `storage_mode` ("static"|"dynamic"|"dual"), `usage` (count + post_count), `attributes` (incl. `source` declarations), and a top-level `guidance` summary grouped by tier. `styles` lists valid is-style-* variations — check it before setting an is-style-* className; `parent`/`ancestor`/`allowed_blocks` are nesting constraints — respect them when nesting. Pass `include_supports:true` for the full supports object. Filters: namespace, category, tier, storage_mode, search (name/title substring), preferred_only, usage_only. Pagination: limit/offset → next_offset. Returns `{block_types[], count, total, offset, next_offset, guidance}`.

tier.description: Exact tier match. Use for migration audits.

storage_mode.description: Filter by storage mode. "dual" surfaces blocks needing both attrs+innerHTML on update.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring match against name + title.

usage_only.description: Only blocks with usage.count > 0 on this site.

include_supports.description: Include each block's full `supports` object. Default false.

tools.name: list_patterns
tools.label: List patterns
tools.description: Block patterns sorted by preference score. Check before building from scratch. Server respects `limit`; `offset` slices client-side. Reference counts are cached for 1 hour — pass `refresh:true` to rebuild. `category` filters differently by pattern kind: registered patterns are matched against their declared pattern categories, while synced patterns (no separate category taxonomy) are matched against the block categories actually used in their content. The response's top-level `categories` lists the registered pattern-category vocabulary.

synced.description: true = synced only, false = registered only, omit = all.

category.description: Filter by pattern category. Registered patterns match declared categories; synced patterns match block categories used in their content.

refresh.description: Bust the 1-hour reference-count cache before listing.

tools.name: get_pattern
tools.label: Get pattern
tools.description: Single pattern's full block content + metadata. Use after list_patterns.

pattern_id.description: Numeric post ID (synced) or registered pattern name.

tools.name: get_site_usage
tools.label: Get site usage
tools.description: Site-wide block + pattern inventory: usage counts, namespace totals, pattern reference counts, legacy patterns.

tools.name: scan_storage_modes
tools.label: Scan storage modes
tools.description: Walk every published post and persist a `block_name → "static"|"dynamic"|"dual"` map (option `gk_block_api_storage_modes`). Slow on large sites; rate-limited to 1/hr. After this runs, get_page_blocks `storage_mode` annotations and dual-storage write enforcement use the live classification. Returns `{scanned_posts, unique_blocks, classification, dual_count, dynamic_count, static_count}`.

tools.name: resolve_url
tools.label: Resolve URL to post
tools.description: URL or path → post ID. Accepts full URLs or site-relative paths. Run this before get_page_blocks / update_block / edit_block_tree when you only have a URL.

tools.name: list_posts
tools.label: List/search posts
tools.description: Search posts by title/content with pagination. Returns `{posts: [{post_id, title, slug, post_type, post_status, post_url, modified}], total, page, per_page, total_pages}`. Use instead of wp post list / wp-json.

search.description: Free-text across title + content. Omit to list.

post_type.description: Single or comma-separated. Default: public types.

post_status.description: publish | draft | private | any | csv. Default: publish. (`any` is exclusive.)

tools.name: get_post_info
tools.label: Get post info
tools.description: Post metadata by post_id, url, or slug+post_type. Returns `{post_id, title, status, post_url, edit_url, modified, created, parent_id, author, mime_type, comment_count}`. Replaces wp eval / get_permalink() shell-outs.

post_id.description: One of post_id, url, or slug.

url.description: Full URL or path. Resolved via url_to_postid.

slug.description: post_name. Combine with post_type for uniqueness.

post_type.description: Scope a slug lookup. Default: any.

tools.name: get_page_blocks
tools.label: Get post blocks
tools.description: Get a post's blocks. Pass post_id OR url (server resolves URL — don't shell out). Returns `{post_id, summary, blocks[], block_count, warnings}`. Each block: `{index (flat), top_level_counter? (top-level only), path, ref (stable gk_ref), name, attributes, innerHTML?, dynamic, storage_mode ("static"|"dynamic"|"dual"), preference? (when non-preferred)}`. Refs survive sibling shifts — pass them to update_block / delete_block / edit_block_tree to chain mutations without re-fetching. Use outline:true or summary_only:true for cheap inspection.

post_id.description: Post ID. Provide either this or url.

url.description: Full URL (https://site.com/path/) or site-relative path (/path/). Resolved via url_to_postid. Provide either this or post_id.

render.description: Expand shortcodes, resolve synced patterns, mark dynamic/static.

search.description: Filter by text in innerHTML. Returns flat matches.

block_name.description: Filter by block name (e.g. "core/button"). Returns flat matches.

outline.description: Return only headings and named sections as a flat outline. Fast page structure view.

summary_only.description: Return only the summary object (no blocks). Fastest page inspection.

include_legacy_paths.description: Add summary.legacy_blocks.paths (per-block path list). Off by default; turn on for migration audits.

persist_refs.description: Default true. When true, missing block refs (attrs.metadata.gk_ref) are assigned and persisted silently (no revision created). Set false for read-only callers that don't want write side effects — refs in the response will not resolve in subsequent mutation calls.

limit.description: Page size: top-level blocks per response. When more remain, the response carries `pagination.next_cursor` — pass it back via `cursor` to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `pagination.next_cursor`. Omit on the first request.

tools.name: get_block
tools.label: Get one block
tools.description: Fetch one block by stable ref OR flat_index — returns the canonical `saved` snapshot (inner_html + attributes) from the database. Same shape that update_block / update_blocks (with `verbose:true`) echo back, so verification reads use the identical contract as the writes that produced them. Lighter than get_page_blocks when you only need to confirm one known block. For dynamic blocks (`saved.is_dynamic`), `inner_html` is the stored template, not rendered output.

ref.description: Stable gk_ref. Provide this OR flat_index.

flat_index.description: Flat block index. Provide this OR ref.

tools.name: update_block
tools.label: Update one block
tools.description: Update one block by flat_index OR by ref (stable gk_ref from get_page_blocks). Provide exactly one targeting field. Refs are recommended for chained mutations because they survive sibling shifts. attributes are SHALLOW-merged at top level — pass full arrays, not deltas. innerHTML replaces atomically. For dual-storage blocks (e.g. yoast/faq-block) you MUST send both fields together; innerHTML-only is rejected. Response includes `saved.inner_html` and `saved.attributes` — the canonical post-save snapshot from the database. Do not fetch the public page to verify edits.

flat_index.description: Zero-based flat `index` from get_page_blocks (counts every block, including innerBlocks). Provide this OR `ref`.

ref.description: Stable gk_ref (e.g. "blk_a3f2c1q9") from get_page_blocks. Survives sibling shifts so chained mutations don't go stale. Provide this OR `flat_index`.

block_name.description: Block type being updated (e.g. "kevinbatdorf/code-block-pro"). Required to activate enrichers — e.g. auto-generating codeHTML from code + language.

attributes.description: Partial attrs (top-level shallow merge). Enrichers derive computed fields (e.g. codeHTML) automatically when block_name is provided.

saved.description: Canonical post-save snapshot of the updated block — exactly what is now in post_content. For dynamic blocks, inner_html is the stored template, not the rendered output.

tools.name: update_blocks
tools.label: Batch-update blocks
tools.description: Update N independent blocks atomically in ONE revision. Each item targets one block by `ref` (recommended) or `flat_index`, with `attributes` and/or `innerHTML`. Validation is all-or-nothing: any stale ref / out-of-range index / dual-storage rejection / duplicate target aborts the batch with itemized errors — no partial writes hit disk. Max 50 items per call. Counts as ONE write against the per-post rate limit. Use this instead of looping update_block when fixing multiple blocks on the same post — keeps revision history clean. Pass `verbose: true` to include `saved.inner_html` + `saved.attributes` per result for per-item verification without a re-read.

updates.description: List of update items (1..50). Each item targets one block; same item shape as update_block.

ref.description: Stable gk_ref. Provide this OR flat_index.

flat_index.description: Flat index from get_page_blocks. Provide this OR ref.

block_name.description: Block type (e.g. "core/paragraph"). Required for enrichers when attributes are provided.

verbose.description: When true, each result includes `saved.inner_html` + `saved.attributes` (the canonical post-save snapshot). Default false to keep batch responses compact.

saved.description: Canonical post-save snapshot. Present only when called with `verbose: true`.

tools.name: insert_blocks
tools.label: Insert blocks
tools.description:
Insert top-level blocks into a post.

POSITIONING — use exactly ONE anchor (any other key, e.g. `after`, `before`, `position`, is rejected):
- `before_ref` / `after_ref` — gk_ref from get_page_blocks. Recommended: refs survive sibling shifts.
- `before_top_level` / `after_top_level` — top_level_counter position.
- Prepend at the very top: `before_top_level: 0`. Append at the end: omit all anchors.

CONTENT — legacy-tier blocks are rejected per the site policy. Blocks with HTML-sourced attributes (e.g. core/paragraph `content`, core/image `url`) must include matching `innerHTML`; attribute-only inserts fail with `inner_html_required`.

VERIFY — the response's inserted[] returns `ref`, `path`, and `top_level_counter`: confirm the block landed where you intended before moving on. The refs let you chain edit_block_tree without re-reading.

after_top_level.description: top_level_counter to insert AFTER (omit or -1 = append). To prepend at the very top, prefer `before_top_level: 0`.

after_ref.description: gk_ref of the top-level block to insert AFTER. Recommended — survives sibling shifts. Takes precedence over after_top_level.

before_ref.description: gk_ref of the top-level block to insert BEFORE. Takes precedence over before_top_level.

blocks.description:
Blocks to insert. Each def nests recursively via `innerBlocks` — build a whole container (group/columns/callout) with its children in this one call; give the container its empty wrapper `innerHTML` (e.g. '
').

innerHTML.description:
Wrapper HTML for container blocks (e.g. "
    "); leaf-block HTML otherwise. REQUIRED when `attributes` includes any source-bound field (rich-text / html / text / raw / attribute / query — e.g. `content` on core/paragraph, `url` on core/image). The server returns `inner_html_required` (HTTP 400) otherwise: an attribute-only insert saves a self-closing block that Gutenberg flags as "Block contains unexpected or invalid content" on next edit.

innerBlocks.description: Child blocks. Nest recursively to build lists, columns, groups, etc.

tools.name: delete_block
tools.label: Delete blocks
tools.description: Remove block(s) by top_level_counter OR by ref. Provide exactly one. For core/block, removes the reference only — not the source pattern.

top_level_counter.description: Zero-based top_level_counter (sequential position among top-level blocks). Provide this OR `ref`.

ref.description: gk_ref of the block to remove (or the leading block if count > 1). Survives sibling shifts. Provide this OR `top_level_counter`.

count.description: Consecutive top-level blocks to remove. Default 1.

tools.name: replace_block_range
tools.label: Replace a range of blocks
tools.description: Atomic single-revision swap of N top-level blocks for M new blocks (M can be 0, 1, or N). Safer than delete+insert (no half-written intermediate state). Distinct from rewrite_post_blocks (which replaces the entire post).

start.description: top_level_counter of first block to replace.

count.description: How many top-level blocks to remove. Pass 0 to insert without removing.

blocks.description: Replacement blocks. May be empty (pure delete) or any length. Each def nests recursively via `innerBlocks` for containers (group/columns/callout) — give the container its empty wrapper `innerHTML`.

innerHTML.description:
Wrapper HTML for container blocks (e.g. "
    "); leaf-block HTML otherwise. REQUIRED when `attributes` includes any source-bound field (rich-text / html / text / raw / attribute / query — e.g. `content` on core/paragraph, `url` on core/image). The server returns `inner_html_required` (HTTP 400) otherwise: an attribute-only insert saves a self-closing block that Gutenberg flags as "Block contains unexpected or invalid content" on next edit.

innerBlocks.description: Child blocks. Nest recursively to build lists, columns, groups, etc.

tools.name: rewrite_post_blocks
tools.label: Rewrite the entire post
tools.description: Replace ALL blocks on a page in one revision. Use for major restructuring; prefer update_block / insert_blocks / replace_block_range for edits.

blocks.description: Complete blocks array (replaces all). Each def nests recursively via `innerBlocks` for containers (group/columns/callout) — give the container its empty wrapper `innerHTML`.

innerHTML.description:
Wrapper HTML for container blocks (e.g. "
    "); leaf-block HTML otherwise. REQUIRED when `attributes` includes any source-bound field (rich-text / html / text / raw / attribute / query — e.g. `content` on core/paragraph, `url` on core/image). The server returns `inner_html_required` (HTTP 400) otherwise: an attribute-only insert saves a self-closing block that Gutenberg flags as "Block contains unexpected or invalid content" on next edit.

innerBlocks.description: Child blocks. Nest recursively to build lists, columns, groups, etc.

tools.name: revert_to_revision
tools.label: Revert post to revision
tools.description: Restore a post to a revision. Pass `before_revision_id` from a prior write to UNDO that write; pass `revision_id` to REDO it.

tools.name: insert_pattern
tools.label: Insert pattern
tools.description: Insert a pattern. Default synced=true inserts a core/block reference (edits to source update all pages); synced=false inlines blocks for per-page edits. NOTE: registered (non-numeric) patterns cannot be synced — server forces synced=false. Response includes `synced` (actual mode used) so you can detect the override.

pattern_id.description: Numeric post ID (synced) or registered pattern name.

after_top_level.description: top_level_counter to insert AFTER. -1/omit = append. Matches insert_blocks naming.

before_top_level.description: top_level_counter to insert BEFORE. Matches insert_blocks naming.

synced.description: true (default) = synced reference; false = inline copy.

tools.name: edit_block_tree
tools.label: Edit block tree
tools.description: Run one structural op on a nested block tree. Ops: update-attrs, update-html, replace-block, remove-block, wrap-in-group, unwrap-group, insert-child, duplicate, move. Target the block via `ref` (stable gk_ref — recommended, survives sibling shifts) OR `path` (integer array, e.g. [0,2,1]). For move, the destination can be a `destination_ref` instead of a path. Creates a revision.

path.description: Target block path (e.g. [0,2,1]). Provide this OR `ref`.

ref.description: Stable gk_ref of the target block. Survives sibling shifts. Provide this OR `path`.

innerHTML.description:
Wrapper HTML for container blocks (e.g. "
    "); leaf-block HTML otherwise. REQUIRED when `attributes` includes any source-bound field (rich-text / html / text / raw / attribute / query — e.g. `content` on core/paragraph, `url` on core/image). The server returns `inner_html_required` (HTTP 400) otherwise: an attribute-only insert saves a self-closing block that Gutenberg flags as "Block contains unexpected or invalid content" on next edit.

innerBlocks.description: Child blocks. Nest recursively to build lists, columns, groups, etc.

block.description: replace-block / insert-child: a block def. Nests recursively via `innerBlocks`; containers need their empty wrapper `innerHTML`.

wrapper.description: wrap-in-group: optional wrapper block. Default core/group.

destination_ref.description: move: destination block ref (alternative to destination).

count.description: move: consecutive blocks to move. Default 1.

ref.description: New ref when the op produced a new block.

tools.name: create_post
tools.label: Create post
tools.description: Create a new post or page. Returns ID, slug, permalink, and edit link. Provide either `content` (raw HTML or block markup) OR `blocks` (structured), not both. Status defaults to draft. Use update_post for trash transitions.

status.description: Initial status. Use update_post for trash transitions.

content.description: Raw post_content (HTML or block markup). Mutually exclusive with blocks.

blocks.description: Structured blocks. Validated against block registry and preference tier — legacy blocks are rejected.

innerHTML.description:
Wrapper HTML for container blocks (e.g. "
    "); leaf-block HTML otherwise. REQUIRED when `attributes` includes any source-bound field (rich-text / html / text / raw / attribute / query — e.g. `content` on core/paragraph, `url` on core/image). The server returns `inner_html_required` (HTTP 400) otherwise: an attribute-only insert saves a self-closing block that Gutenberg flags as "Block contains unexpected or invalid content" on next edit.

innerBlocks.description: Child blocks. Nest recursively to build lists, columns, groups, etc.

parent.description: Parent post ID (hierarchical post types only).

featured_media.description: Attachment ID. Must be an image MIME. Send 0 to leave unset.

terms.description: Map of taxonomy slug → term IDs. For non-built-in taxonomies on CPTs.

author.description: User ID. Other-user authorship requires edit_others_posts cap.

tools.name: update_post
tools.label: Update post
tools.description: Partial update of post metadata, status, or terms. Block content edits stay on the per-block tools. Use status: "trash" to trash; any non-trash status untrashes a trashed post. At least one mutating field besides post_id is required.

tools.name: list_terms
tools.label: List terms
tools.description: List terms in a taxonomy (default: category). Useful for discovering category and tag IDs to pass to create_post or update_post.

tools.name: upload_media
tools.label: Upload media
tools.description: Upload an item to the WordPress media library. Provide exactly one of: `path` (local filesystem on the MCP host, sent as multipart), `url` (server-side sideload, 25 MB cap), or `data_base64` (with `filename`). Returns the attachment ID and URL ready for core/image blocks.

path.description: Absolute path on the MCP host. Will be read and POSTed as multipart.

url.description: Public URL the WordPress site can fetch.

alt_text.description: Saved as _wp_attachment_image_alt meta. Critical for accessibility.

post_id.description: Attach to a parent post (sets post_parent).

tools.name: yoast_get_seo
tools.label: Get Yoast SEO metadata
tools.description: Read all Yoast SEO metadata for a post or page (title, description, robots, Open Graph, Twitter card, schema types, cornerstone flag, breadcrumb, redirect, scores, primary terms).

tools.name: yoast_update_seo
tools.label: Update Yoast SEO metadata
tools.description: Update one or more Yoast SEO fields on a single post or page. Only supplied fields are written. `noindex` is tri-state (true / false / null).

noindex.description: true=noindex, false=explicit index. Pass null to reset to the post-type default; omit to leave the current value unchanged. (Advertised as a single boolean type because some AI clients — e.g. Google Gemini — reject a "null" member in a type array; the handler still accepts an explicit null.)

og_image_id.description: Attachment ID for the OG image.

twitter_image_id.description: Attachment ID for the Twitter image.

primary_terms.description: { taxonomy_name: term_id } — set primary term per taxonomy.

tools.name: yoast_bulk_update_seo
tools.label: Bulk-update Yoast SEO metadata
tools.description: Update Yoast SEO fields on multiple posts in one call. Each item must include `post_id` plus any fields to update. Response preserves order.

posts.description: Array of objects, each with post_id and fields to update.

noindex.description: true=noindex, false=explicit index. Pass null to reset to the post-type default; omit to leave the current value unchanged. (Advertised as a single boolean type because some AI clients — e.g. Google Gemini — reject a "null" member in a type array; the handler still accepts an explicit null.)

og_image_id.description: Attachment ID for the OG image.

twitter_image_id.description: Attachment ID for the Twitter image.

primary_terms.description: { taxonomy_name: term_id } — set primary term per taxonomy.

tools.name: site_editor_context
tools.label: Site editor context
tools.description: Get the site's design tokens (theme name plus the color, gradient, font-size, and spacing presets) so block markup references theme-aligned preset slugs (e.g. has-primary-color) rather than hard-coded values.
